title: lquery level with enough OR-variants wraps a uint16 totallen, ~65 KB -- leaves its block
live_proof: upstream 8c34261109, "ltree: Fix overflows with lquery parsing", absent at the 17.5 pin. Upstream: a single lquery level with many OR-separated variants overflows totallen, which is a uint16, because each variant contributes MAXALIGN(LVAR_HDRSIZE + len); once it wraps, the data written by LQL_NEXT() is corrupt and the access goes out of bounds. The trigger here is 66 variants of 1000 characters, about 66 KB against a uint16 ceiling of 65535. Independently established on the pin by host ASan (heap-buffer-overflow in the lquery path) and by the purecap arm, which raises SIGPROT on both builds.
fidelity: real server, real allocator, in a contrib extension rather than core. ~65 KB, so it leaves its block

cheribsd-revocation.oracle: SIGPROT on the plain purecap build -- CHERI-DETECTED (2026-10-04). SIGPROT(34) on both purecap builds. ~65 KB, leaves the malloc block.
cheribsd-revocation.run: defect and control run 2026-10-10 by shared/run-cheribsd.sh against the same deployed purecap tree
cheribsd-revocation.verdict_note: Attributed by its own control and by the threshold, bisected in the guest with one backend per input: CREATE EXTENSION ltree alone, and 2, 32 and 63 variants, all exit 0; 64 and 66 variants both exit 162 (SIGPROT). A variant costs 1024 bytes on this build, read back in band as the difference between pg_column_size of a 2-variant and a 3-variant lquery (2080 -> 3104), so 64 is the first count that wraps. The installed pg_config.h in the guest says MAXIMUM_ALIGNOF 8, which is not what the deployed ltree behaves as.

virtual-malloc.oracle: virtual profile, PostgreSQL's contexts stock (tools/arms.json virtual-mallocng): a fault after the trigger started that its control.sql or a justified fault_sites ties to the defect, or the trigger completes and this arm did not see it
virtual-malloc.verdict_note: cause=28 pc=0x3fa3001c7c in memcpy; by control: control.sql (the statement below the threshold) completed on this image

virtual-pg-pools.oracle: virtual profile with the memory-context port's patch 0003: every palloc chunk a child lifetime of its block (CDERIVE), revoked by pfree and repalloc (CREVOKE) (tools/arms.json virtual-mallocng-pg-pools): as virtual-malloc
virtual-pg-pools.verdict_note: cause=28 pc=0x3f84001c7c in memcpy; by control: control.sql (the statement below the threshold) completed on this image

status: measured on virtual Capstone (virtual-malloc, virtual-pg-pools) and stock CheriBSD (cheribsd-revocation); each arm's verdict_from names its bundle. The physical spatial/sublet pair measured 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-10 stays in results/
note: The 2026-10-05 spatial and sublet runs are WITHDRAWN and carry no verdict. Both recorded silent on an image that did not contain ltree. A domain cannot dlopen, so an extension reaches it only by being linked in (patch 0015, ports/postgres/app/toolchain/static_modules.c), and the MODULES list of ports/postgres/app/build-domain.sh named only dict_snowball and plpgsql; the guest share directory likewise held plpgsql.control alone. The trigger's first statement, CREATE EXTENSION ltree, therefore failed on the missing control file and the lquery cast never executed. A control failure, so both arms are out of their denominators until they are rerun. build-domain.sh now links ltree, pg_trgm and fuzzystrmatch and stages their control and version scripts; both arm images were rebuilt on 2026-10-06 and carry six modules.
nested_why: The object is a palloc chunk, which AllocSet carves out of a block it took from malloc, so the defect is nested by the allocator that served it.
